record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Stochastic programming for forestry depends on a scenario set that is rich enough to represent uncertainty in prices, demand, growth, disasters, and operations, but small enough that the resulting model remains solvable. The open question is how to construct scenario representations for strategic, tactical, or operational forestry problems that capture the essential uncertainty without making the optimization intractable.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 26 How can we represent uncertainty through scenarios for strategic, tactical or operational problems in forestry so that the underlying uncertainty is well represented in a solvable model?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multistage stochastic optimization problem arising in forest management at one of three planning levels: strategic (long-horizon decisions such as land use, road network design, and sustainable harvest levels), tactical (medium-horizon decisions such as annual harvest scheduling and transportation planning), or operational (short-horizon decisions such as daily crew assignment, bucking, and routing). The uncertainty in such a problem may involve any combination of: timber and product prices, product demand, biological growth and yield, natural disasters (fire, wind, pests, disease), and operational factors (machine availability, weather, productivity).

Formally, let the underlying uncertainty be modeled by a stochastic process ξ = (ξ_1, …, ξ_T) on a probability space (Ω, F, P), and let the optimization problem be of the form

   min_{x ∈ X} E_ξ[ f(x, ξ) ],

subject to nonanticipativity and possibly multistage recourse constraints, where X encodes feasibility (resource, ecological, logistical) and f is a forestry-specific cost or negative-value functional.

A scenario representation replaces ξ by a finite tree {ξ^s, p_s}_{s=1}^S with S scenarios and probabilities p_s, giving the deterministic equivalent

   min_{x ∈ X} Σ_{s=1}^S p_s f(x, ξ^s).

Develop a methodology for constructing such a scenario set {(ξ^s, p_s)} for strategic, tactical, and operational forestry problems that simultaneously:

  (a) captures the essential features of the joint distribution of prices, demand, growth, disasters, and operational uncertainty (e.g., in terms of moments, tail behavior, temporal/spatial dependence, or a probability metric such as Wasserstein or nested distance from the true process),

  (b) yields a deterministic equivalent that is computationally tractable on instances of realistic size, and

  (c) admits quantitative guarantees relating the optimal value and optimal first-stage decisions of the scenario-based problem to those of the true stochastic problem.

The problem is to give a constructive procedure—together with conditions under which the above three requirements can be met—for representing uncertainty by scenarios in strategic, tactical, and operational forestry optimization.
artifact.status_search_result: Scenario generation for multistage stochastic programming is an active area (stability bounds, scenario reduction, nested-distance methods), and applications to forestry under price, growth, and disaster uncertainty continue to appear, but no general-purpose method that simultaneously guarantees representativeness, tractability, and solution-quality bounds for strategic/tactical/operational forestry problems has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Scenario generation for multistage stochastic programming (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys scenario generation methods and notes that no method is universally best; trade-offs between fidelity and tractability remain.
status_evidence.claim: General scenario-generation methodology with the desired guarantees is not settled, supporting open status.
